rationale: Both candidates align well to the target (trait_efo=alcohol dependence; phenotyping_reported=Alcohol use disorder) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we rely on structural and effect-size evidence. PGS002738 is a genome-wide PRS-CS score with far broader variant coverage (326,000 vs 858 for PGS002739’s gene-based PRS-CSx), which is generally a stronger structural signal for a polygenic disorder when comparable PRS-only metrics are absent. It also shows a slightly stronger discrimination proxy in the selected validation (OR top 10% vs rest 1.96 [1.54–2.51] vs 1.76 [1.32–2.34]). PGS002739’s main advantage is AFR-only evaluation (ancestry match for African American validation), but without a specified deployment ancestry and with weaker OR plus much sparser construction, PGS002738 is better supported overall on the visible fields.

PGS004913 has cleaner endpoint fidelity to the target: both trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are explicitly “Alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis,” matching the alcoholic liver cirrhosis concept, whereas PGS001777’s phenotyping_reported is “Cirrhosis (males),” introducing a sex-restricted phenotype mismatch despite a similar trait_reported label. Neither candidate reports PRS-only AUC/R², so PGS001777’s AUROC=0.671 is a full-model metric and not comparable as PRS evidence; in that setting, PGS004913’s stronger structural PRS construction (20 variants vs 3) and disease-focused design among heavy drinkers with stated basic covariates (age, sex, PCs) is better-supported than PGS001777’s unknown covariates and sparse 3-variant score. Both are EUR-only, so ancestry does not differentiate.

PGS001135 is better supported on PRS-comparable evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC (0.539) and PGS-only R² (0.00291), allowing a clean PRS signal check (and it stays below the arthritis heritability ceiling). It also uses only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array) and has multi-ancestry evaluation (AFR/EAS/EUR/SAS), which is supportive for transportability. In contrast, PGS004547 has a more specific ICD10-like endpoint label (M13 Other arthritis) and a large genome-wide variant set, but it provides no AUROC/R² at all (only an OR=1.26, which is weak-to-moderate) and has unknown covariates with EUR-only evaluation, making its standalone PRS performance less verifiable from the visible fields.

Both candidates are near-clones from the same pan-trait UKB snpnet framework paper with identical training cohort (UKB), training N (269,704), covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), ancestry distribution, and validation size (24,905), so endpoint/transportability evidence is essentially tied. The only meaningful differentiators are (i) endpoint fidelity: PGS001261 is explicitly "Angina pectoris (time-to-event)" with phenotyping_reported "TTE angina pectoris" vs PGS001260’s more generic "Angina" label, and (ii) slightly stronger PRS-comparable metrics for PGS001261 (PGS-only AUROC 0.58233; PGS-only R2 0.01228) than PGS001260 (0.58108; 0.01185). Differences are very small, hence low confidence, but they consistently favor PGS001261.

PGS005254 is the better-supported match to the target trait aortic stenosis: it has exact trait alignment (trait_reported and trait_efo both aortic stenosis) whereas PGS005255 is primarily a hemodynamic measurement score (trait_reported: mean pressure gradient; trait_efo includes aortic measurement), making it less endpoint-faithful despite sharing the same phenotyping_reported (incident aortic stenosis). Both candidates are otherwise near-clones (same publication, PRS-CS, EUR-only dev/eval, same covariates, same validation N), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2; in that setting, the stronger effect-size evidence and training support favor PGS005254 (HR 1.64 vs 1.53; larger training n=205,483 vs 98,645).

PGS004913 is better supported for the specific target of alcoholic liver cirrhosis because it is explicitly disease-focused on alcohol-associated cirrhosis among heavy drinkers, with tightly aligned trait_reported/phenotyping_reported and a strong PRS effect-size signal (OR top vs bottom deciles = 4.4) under basic covariates (age, sex, PCs). PGS000704 matches the EFO label but comes from a broad UKB biomarker genetics framework context and only reports a full-model C-index (0.711) plus a modest HR=1.18, with no PRS-only AUC/R2; the full-model metric is not PRS-comparable and is likely covariate-driven. Both are EUR-focused, but PGS004913’s endpoint fidelity and stronger genetic risk separation outweigh PGS000704’s larger training/validation sizes.

PGS001268 is better supported on PRS-comparable performance evidence for ankylosing spondylitis: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.7346 and PGS-only R²=0.10232 (with CIs for AUROC), whereas PGS002089 provides no PRS-only AUROC/R² and only a partial correlation (partial-r=0.0919), which is less directly comparable for PRS discrimination. Endpoint alignment is acceptable for both (same EFO), but PGS001268’s time-to-event phenotyping is a mild mismatch versus PGS002089’s direct disease label; this is outweighed by PGS001268’s much clearer PRS-only metrics and larger evaluation sample (67,425 vs 18,262). Both are UKB-based framework-style scores, but PGS001268’s reported PRS-only metrics and basic covariates make it the stronger evidenced candidate here.

Both candidates map to the correct EFO (alcoholic liver cirrhosis), but PGS000704 has stronger structural support and cleaner disclosed modeling context: it is a genome-wide snpnet multi-PRS with 183,271 variants, explicit basic covariates (age as time scale, sex, batch, PCs), large training (UKB) and large validation (n=135,300) with some non-EUR evaluation (MAE 33%). PGS001777 is a very sparse 3-variant score with unknown covariates and a much smaller validation (n=1,390); its reported AUROC (0.671) is full-model and not PRS-only, and its phenotyping_reported is restricted ('Cirrhosis (males)') despite the target being generic alcoholic cirrhosis. Since neither provides PRS-only AUC/R2, the more robust genome-wide construction and clearer covariate disclosure in PGS000704 outweigh the small full-model AUROC difference (0.711 vs 0.671).

Both candidates match the target trait (AAA) well by trait_reported/trait_efo, but PGS000753 has stronger endpoint fidelity and disease-focused support: it comes from an AAA-specific genetic architecture study (MVP/MAYO-VDB) and explicitly uses a prevalent AAA diagnosis endpoint, with a moderate per-SD effect size (OR=1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) under basic covariates (age/sex/PCs). In contrast, PGS002054 is from a UK Biobank-wide portability framework paper; while it is genome-wide (LDpred2, 592k variants) and reports a PRS-comparable partial correlation (0.0144), that metric is very small and the model is embedded in a generic portability setting with heavier covariate adjustment (adds deprivation index and more PCs), offering weaker disease-specific evidence. With no PGS-only AUC/R2 for either, the disease-focused endpoint + interpretable effect-size evidence favors PGS000753 over the framework-derived PGS002054.

Both candidates are near-clones from the same UKB pan-trait sparse snpnet framework (same publication, training n=269,704, 10 variants, identical covariates, identical ancestry distribution, same validation n=67,425), so the main differentiator is endpoint fidelity and PRS-only metrics. PGS001267 matches the target trait directly in both trait_reported and phenotyping_reported ("Ankylosing spondylitis"), whereas PGS001268 is explicitly time-to-event ("TTE ankylosing spondylitis" / "time-to-event"), which is a mild endpoint mismatch for a generic ankylosing spondylitis target. Although PGS001268 has slightly higher PRS-only AUROC/R² (0.7346/0.1023 vs 0.7265/0.0988), the gap is small and does not outweigh the cleaner phenotype alignment of PGS001267.

Both candidates match the target endpoint cleanly (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all abdominal aortic aneurysm) and neither shows obvious clinical-risk packaging in covariates (both are basic demographics + PCs). The key differentiator is PRS-comparable performance evidence: PGS001784 reports a PRS-only/covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.014661, whereas PGS002054 does not report PRS-only AUC/R2 and only provides a partial correlation (partial-r=0.0144), which is less directly comparable as a PRS performance metric. PGS001784 is also developed across multiple biobanks (global biobank framework) with a larger genome-wide variant set (911,440 vs 592,187), while PGS002054 is a UKB-only portability framework score; despite PGS002054 having multi-ancestry evaluation records, its visible selected validation is European and it lacks cleaner PRS-only metrics. Overall, PGS001784 has slightly stronger, more interpretable PRS-only performance support on the record.

Both candidates match the target trait well (trait_reported/trait_efo are aortic stenosis; both use incident aortic stenosis endpoints; both DEV/EVAL are EUR only) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we must lean on effect-size evidence and covariate comparability. PGS005254 reports a clear per-SD HR=1.64 with CI (1.50–1.78) under a relatively clean covariate set (age, age^2, sex, PCs), making the genetic signal more interpretable as PRS-driven. PGS005252 reports a higher HR point estimate (1.92) but without CI and its only discrimination metric is a full-model C-index=0.87 alongside a very heavy comorbidity/clinical covariate bundle (T2D, HTN, CAD, hyperlipidemia, BMI, smoking, renal failure), which strongly suggests the 0.87 is covariate-driven and not comparable as PRS evidence. Given cleaner evaluation framing and more complete effect-size reporting, PGS005254 is better-supported on the visible fields.

Both candidates match the target endpoint cleanly (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all ankylosing spondylitis) and use only basic covariates (no obvious clinical-risk packaging). PGS001267 is better-supported on PRS-comparable performance: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.7265 and PGS-only R²=0.0988 in Europeans, whereas PGS002089 provides no PGS-only AUROC/R² (only a partial correlation of 0.0919), making cross-model PRS performance comparison weaker. Although PGS002089 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach with many variants (22,026) and has some multi-ancestry evaluation, the lack of standard PRS-only metrics on the record leaves it less directly evidenced than PGS001267’s clearly reported PRS-only discrimination.

PGS005252 is the better-supported match to the target trait (aortic stenosis): its trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are directly aligned to incident aortic stenosis, whereas PGS005255 is primarily reported as a valve-function measurement (mean pressure gradient) with a broader/mixed trait_efo despite mentioning incident aortic stenosis in phenotyping. Neither candidate reports PRS-comparable metrics (pgs_only_auc/r2 are null), so we rely on endpoint fidelity and available effect-size evidence; PGS005252 shows a stronger HR per SD (1.92 vs 1.53 for PGS005255). Although PGS005252’s full-model C-index=0.87 is not PRS-only and is likely covariate-influenced (it uses many clinical covariates), it still provides some performance context; PGS005255 provides no discrimination metric at all. Training/validation are both EUR-only; validation N is larger for PGS005252 (446,895 vs 244,450), but this is only a weak tie-break. Overall, PGS005252 has cleaner trait alignment and stronger effect-size support than PGS005255.

PGS002739 is the better-supported match to the target trait alcohol dependence because its endpoint is directly aligned across fields (trait_reported: Alcohol use disorder; trait_efo: alcohol dependence; phenotyping_reported: Alcohol use disorder), whereas PGS000201 is framed as “Problematic alcohol use” with an EFO of “alcohol dependence measurement” and a DSM-5 criteria count (log-transformed), which is a more quantitative/problem-use construct rather than a straightforward dependence diagnosis. Neither record reports PRS-only AUC/R2, but PGS002739 provides a clear case-control discrimination signal (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.76), while PGS000201 only shows a small incremental ΔR² vs covariates (0.01192) and a beta on a transformed count outcome, which is harder to compare to dependence risk. Although PGS000201 has explicit basic covariates and a large genome-wide variant set, PGS002739’s phenotype fidelity and interpretable risk stratification evidence outweigh the covariate-unknown penalty here.

Both candidates match the target trait well (same trait_reported/trait_efo; phenotyping is direct AAA, with PGS000753 explicitly “prevalent” and PGS001784 generic). The key differentiator is PRS-comparable performance evidence: PGS001784 reports a PRS-only/covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.014661 (and a full-model AUROC=0.868, which is not treated as PRS-only), whereas PGS000753 provides no AUC/R2 at all and only a moderate OR=1.37 per SD. PGS001784 also has stronger structural properties (PRS-CS-auto, genome-wide 911,440 variants) versus PGS000753’s sparse P+T 29-variant score, which is generally less able to capture polygenic signal. Covariates are basic in both (PGS001784 is heavier but still demographic/PC terms), so they don’t negate the advantage of having explicit PRS-only R2 plus a more comprehensive model.

PGS001135 is better supported on PRS-comparable evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC (0.539) and PGS-only R² (0.00291), allowing a clean PRS signal check (and it stays well below the provided heritability ceiling). It also has basic, non-leaky covariates (age/sex/PCs/array) and broader evaluation ancestry coverage (AFR/EAS/EUR/SAS), which is supportive for transportability. In contrast, PGS004477 has no AUROC/R² reported at all (only an OR=1.20, which indicates weak PRS discrimination), unknown covariates, and EUR-only evaluation; despite its genome-wide variant count, the missing PRS-comparable metrics and weaker effect-size evidence make it less well supported here.

PGS002738 is the better-supported match to the target trait alcohol dependence because its endpoint fields are directly aligned: trait_efo is exactly “alcohol dependence” and both trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are “Alcohol use disorder,” a close clinical synonym. It also shows a stronger discrimination signal via an OR(top 10% vs rest)=1.96 (1.54–2.51), which is meaningful effect-size evidence when PRS-only AUC/R2 are absent for both candidates. In contrast, PGS000201 is mapped to “alcohol dependence measurement” and reported as “Problematic alcohol use,” with phenotyping reported as a DSM-5 criteria count (log-transformed), which is a more quantitative/problem-use construct rather than a direct dependence diagnosis; its only PRS-comparable metric is a small ΔR²=0.01192. Both are EUR-evaluated with similar validation N (~7.6–7.9k) and same method (PRS-CS), so the decision is driven mainly by endpoint fidelity and stronger effect-size evidence favoring PGS002738.

Both candidates are from the same pan-trait UKB snpnet framework paper, use the same basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), have identical ancestry distribution patterns (DEV EUR; EVAL multi-ancestry with selected EUR), and report clean PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²). Endpoint-wise, PGS001261 is a time-to-event angina phenotype (a mild mismatch risk for a generic angina target), while PGS001262 is a direct doctor-diagnosed angina endpoint, which is more straightforwardly aligned to ‘angina pectoris’. On PRS-only performance, PGS001262 is slightly better (PGS-only AUROC 0.58683 vs 0.58233; PGS-only R² 0.01304 vs 0.01228), and both are plausible under the heritability ceiling. Although PGS001261 has more variants and larger training N, those are weaker signals here than endpoint fidelity plus the (small but consistent) PRS-only metric advantage for PGS001262.

Both candidates are near-clones from the same UKB pan-trait snpnet framework paper with identical trait_efo (angina pectoris), similar basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), and the same ancestry setup (DEV EUR; EVAL multi-ancestry with selected EUR performance). With endpoint fidelity essentially equivalent (PGS001262: doctor-diagnosed angina wording; PGS001260: angina), the main differentiator is PRS-comparable performance: PGS001262 has slightly higher PGS-only AUROC (0.58683 vs 0.58108) and PGS-only R2 (0.01304 vs 0.01185). Both R2 values are below the local h2_obs ceiling (~0.009–0.014 range depending on definition) but are close enough that neither is clearly implausible; the small metric edge favors PGS001262. PGS001260’s larger training N and higher variant count are weaker signals here and do not outweigh the better PRS-only metrics in PGS001262.

Both candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity and study context: same reported phenotype (M13 Other arthritis), same EFO mapping (arthritis), same UKB training cohort, identical training (n=174,489) and validation size (n=56,192), and EUR-only development/evaluation. Neither reports PRS-comparable AUC/R2 (PGS-only metrics are null), so performance must be inferred from the available effect size. PGS004547 shows a stronger per-SD odds ratio (OR=1.262198) than PGS004477 (OR=1.1956), which is the only differentiating empirical signal here; method differences are secondary within the same publication family when effect-size evidence differs.

Both candidates align well to the target trait (trait_efo=asthma) and use only basic covariates (no obvious clinical-risk packaging). However, PGS001344 provides clean PRS-comparable performance metrics in Europeans (PGS-only AUROC=0.64568; PGS-only R2=0.05973), which are interpretable and below the asthma liability h2 ceiling (0.1515). In contrast, PGS002061 reports no PRS-only AUC/R2 and only a partial correlation (partial-r=0.1184), making its predictive strength harder to compare directly despite larger variant count and broader evaluation ancestries. Given the domain guidance to prioritize endpoint fidelity plus comparable PRS-only metrics, PGS001344 is better-supported on the visible fields.

PGS002727 is better supported for the target trait asthma because it comes from a disease-focused pediatric asthma study and provides a strong PRS-discrimination signal via an effect size (OR per SD=1.57) alongside reported AUROC/R² (though these appear to be full-model and thus not PRS-comparable). It is also evaluated very broadly across ancestries (AFR/AMR/EAS/EUR/SAS) with a very large validation sample (n=391,820), supporting transportability. In contrast, PGS002061 is from a UKB portability framework paper (a known weaker archetype when a disease-focused alternative exists) and reports only a modest PRS-comparable metric (partial-r=0.1184) without OR/HR or PRS-only AUC/R²; its evaluation sample is much smaller (n=19,551) and development is EUR-only. Endpoint fidelity is acceptable for both (asthma), but PGS002727 has stronger disease-specific context and stronger effect-size evidence than the framework-derived PGS002061.

Both candidates align well to the target (atrial flutter) via identical trait_efo and very similar trait_reported/phenotyping_reported, though PGS001339 is explicitly time-to-event (a mild endpoint penalty). The decisive difference is performance evidence: PGS001339 reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.613 and PGS-only R2=0.02447), which are interpretable and pass the heritability ceiling sanity check (h2_obs≈0.0157; R2 is small and not implausibly inflated). PGS002050 provides only partial correlation (partial-r=0.1034) and has no PRS-only AUROC/R2, making its predictive strength less directly comparable for PRS selection. While PGS002050 has a stronger structural setup (LDpred2 with many more variants and larger training N), the lack of PRS-comparable discrimination metrics on the record leaves it less well-supported than PGS001339 on visible evidence.

PGS001263 is the better-supported match for the target trait atrial flutter because its endpoint is directly aligned: trait_reported, trait_efo, and phenotyping_reported are all specifically “Atrial flutter,” whereas PGS001339 is a combined and time-to-event phenotype (“Atrial fibrillation and flutter (time-to-event)” / “TTE atrial fibrillation and flutter”), which is a less faithful endpoint for a generic atrial flutter target. On PRS-comparable metrics, both are near-identical and cleanly reported (PGS-only AUROC/R2 present with only basic covariates), but PGS001263 is slightly higher (PGS-only AUROC 0.61716 vs 0.613; PGS-only R2 0.02517 vs 0.02447). Training/validation size and study family are the same, so phenotype fidelity plus the small PRS-only metric edge favors PGS001263.

Both candidates match the target trait cleanly (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all atrial fibrillation) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model AUC/C-index values are not directly comparable as PRS metrics. PGS005168 is strongly penalized for explicit clinical risk-calculator packaging via covariates including CHARGE-AF (plus age/age^2/sex/array), making its high C-index=0.8718 likely covariate-driven and weak evidence about standalone PRS quality. PGS005313 uses only basic covariates (age, sex), avoiding that major leakage signal, and it also shows a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.82) alongside a large genome-wide PRS-CSx model (1,271,239 variants) and multi-ancestry evaluation context. Given cleaner covariates and stronger structural/effect-size support, PGS005313 is better-supported on the visible fields.

Both candidates match the target trait cleanly (trait_reported/efo/phenotyping_reported all atrial fibrillation). However, PGS005168’s only discrimination metric is a full-model C-index 0.8718 and it explicitly includes CHARGE-AF in covariates, which is a named clinical risk calculator and strongly suggests risk-wrapper packaging; without any PGS-only AUC/R2 or incremental metric, its high C-index is not interpretable as PRS strength. PGS002814 also lacks PGS-only metrics, but its covariates are basic (age, sex, 20 PCs) and it provides a strong per-SD effect size (OR≈1.94), which is direct evidence of PRS discrimination and less likely to be covariate-inflated. Despite being evaluated only in East Asians and using a sparser P+T score, the cleaner covariate context plus strong OR makes PGS002814 better-supported than the CHARGE-AF-packaged PGS005168.

PGS001263 is the better-supported choice for the target trait atrial flutter because it has exact endpoint alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all “Atrial flutter”) and reports clean PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.617 and PGS-only R²=0.025), which can be sanity-checked against the heritability ceiling and interpreted without relying on covariate-boosted full-model metrics. In contrast, PGS002050 uses a broader combined endpoint (“Atrial fibrillation and flutter”) rather than flutter-specific, and it lacks PRS-only AUROC/R² entirely—only a partial correlation is provided—making its predictive evidence less directly comparable for PRS quality despite larger variant count and training N.

PGS001344 is better supported on PRS-comparable performance: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.64568 and PGS-only R²=0.05973 (no covariates), enabling clean comparison and a heritability-ceiling sanity check, whereas PGS002727 lacks any PGS-only AUC/R² and only provides full-model AUROC=0.66/R²=0.04 which is not a valid substitute for PRS-only performance. Endpoint alignment is acceptable for both (asthma), but PGS002727 is pediatric-asthma-specific (more restricted to a subtype/age group) while PGS001344 targets general doctor-diagnosed asthma, closer to the generic ‘asthma’ target. Although PGS002727 is disease-focused and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method with many variants plus a strong OR per SD (1.57), the absence of PRS-only metrics makes its support weaker than PGS001344’s directly comparable PRS-only metrics with basic covariates.

Both candidates match the target endpoint cleanly (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all atrial fibrillation) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model AUROC values (0.78 for PGS005313 vs 0.74 for PGS002814) are not strong cross-model PRS evidence. With PRS-only metrics absent, structural and transportability signals dominate: PGS005313 uses a genome-wide shrinkage cross-ancestry method (PRS-CSx) with far broader genome coverage (1,271,239 variants vs 4,520) and is evaluated across multiple ancestries, whereas PGS002814 is a sparse P+T score evaluated only in East Asians. Both have strong per-SD ORs, but PGS005313’s combination of method/variant breadth and multi-ancestry evaluation provides better-supported robustness than PGS002814’s single-ancestry evaluation and sparse construction.

Both candidates are near-clones: identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (basal cell carcinoma), same publication family, same EUR-only ancestry distribution, same training cohort (MGI) and training N (11,734), same covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4), and same validation N (11,322). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model AUROC=0.632 is not a differentiator. The only visible empirical edge is slightly stronger reported performance for PGS000454 (Nagelkerke R² 0.0489 vs 0.0487; OR top 1% vs rest 3.79 vs 3.61) with essentially identical per-SD OR/Beta, so PGS000454 wins but the margin is minimal.

Both candidates are near-clones: same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (basal cell carcinoma), same method (GWAS Hits), same EUR-only ancestry across GWAS/DEV/EVAL, same training cohort (MGI) and training/validation sizes, and same basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model AUROC differences are not strong PRS differentiators. With endpoints and design effectively identical, PGS000452 has a marginally higher full-model AUROC (0.632 vs 0.630) and higher Nagelkerke R² (0.0487 vs 0.0456), while PGS000456 only has a slightly higher top-1% OR. Overall evidence is essentially tied, but the small edge in the reported discrimination metrics favors PGS000452.

PGS002755 is a direct atopic dermatitis/atopic eczema score with an incident AD endpoint and a PRS-comparable effect size reported (HR high vs low PRS=1.249, 95% CI 1.123–1.391) in a very large EUR evaluation sample (n=337,910), and it uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS; ~1.09M variants), which is structurally better suited to a polygenic trait than a 25-variant hits-only score. PGS001773 targets a narrower phenotype (moderate-to-severe AD) and its only reported discrimination metrics are full-model AUROC=0.93 and R²=0.49 (not PGS-only), which are non-comparable and also implausibly high relative to the eczema heritability ceiling, suggesting covariate-driven inflation; it also has much smaller validation (n=676) and includes parental ethnicity covariates that further confound interpretation. Overall, PGS002755 has cleaner, more credible PRS evidence despite both lacking explicit PGS-only AUC/R².

Both candidates are near-clones: identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (basal cell carcinoma), same publication family, same EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL ancestry, same training cohort (MGI) and training/validation sample sizes, and similarly basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model AUROC differences are not strong PRS-comparable evidence. With endpoints and covariates effectively identical, PGS000454 has a marginally higher full-model AUROC (0.632 vs 0.630) and higher Nagelkerke R² (0.0489 vs 0.0456), while PGS000456 only slightly improves the top-1% OR. Given these tiny, mostly full-model metric differences, the edge for PGS000454 is slight and confidence is low.

PGS004587 is the better-supported match to the target trait (atopic eczema) because its endpoint is a generic atopic dermatitis diagnosis framed as incident disease (phenotyping_reported: "Incident atopic dermatitis"), aligning more directly with broad atopic eczema risk than PGS001773’s restricted subtype endpoint ("Moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis"). Neither candidate reports PRS-only AUC/R², so PGS001773’s very high AUROC=0.93 and R²=0.49 are full-model metrics (and implausibly high relative to the eczema heritability ceiling), making them non-comparable and potentially covariate/packaging-driven; by contrast PGS004587 provides at least a PRS-stratified HR (1.153 high vs low) in a very large EUR evaluation (n=337,910) with non-clinical covariates. Overall, PGS004587 has cleaner phenotype fidelity to the generic target and avoids relying on suspect full-model discrimination, but the lack of PRS-only metrics in both keeps confidence low.

PGS000327 has clean endpoint fidelity: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to autism spectrum disorder, whereas PGS002790 has an explicit phenotype mismatch (phenotyping_reported = "Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)") despite the ASD label. On performance evidence, neither reports PRS-only AUC/R², but PGS000327 provides a stronger disease-relevant effect size (OR=1.33 per SD) and a higher reported R² (0.0245 vs partial R²=0.00546 for PGS002790), both well below the ASD heritability ceiling and thus plausible. PGS000327 also comes from an ASD-focused GWAS paper with explicit training size and broader cohort list, while PGS002790 lacks training sample size and appears embedded in a broader cross-trait study context, making its ASD score less directly supported.

Both candidates match the target trait well (trait_efo=atopic eczema; phenotyping_reported=incident atopic dermatitis), use the same covariates, and have the same EUR evaluation ancestry and validation sample size (n=337,910). Neither reports PRS-comparable AUC/R2, so performance can’t be separated by clean discrimination metrics; both only provide a modest HR (PGS002755 HR=1.249 vs PGS004587 HR=1.153). With metrics essentially tied/limited, structural signals dominate: PGS002755 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS) with ~1.09M variants, which is generally better suited to a polygenic trait than PGS004587’s 23 genome-wide significant SNPs. PGS004587’s listed training cohorts (EB/FinnGen/UKB) are supportive but don’t outweigh the much stronger genome-wide model structure given the lack of PRS-only metrics.

Both candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity and study context: same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (Disorders of bilirubin excretion; bilirubin metabolism disease), same UKB-only training (n=391,124), same covariates (sex, age, birth date, deprivation index, 16 PCs), same ancestry distribution and validation size (n=19,924), and essentially identical PRS-comparable performance evidence (partial-r=0.0716 with overlapping CIs). PGS004546 has tighter endpoint fidelity to the target trait: trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are explicitly ICD10 K80 (Cholelithiasis) with trait_efo exactly cholelithiasis, whereas PGS002072 uses a broader composite phenotype (“Cholelithiasis and cholecystitis”) and even maps trait_efo to both conditions. PGS001301 is better supported on PRS-comparable performance: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.82867 and PGS-only R²=0.14224 (with basic covariates listed separately), enabling a cleaner assessment of the genetic score contribution and staying below the provided liability-scale heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.2305).
